channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia leaving the US, self-deporting to Spain
item.description: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, who was returned to the U.S. after being mistakenly deported to a Salvadoran mega-prison, is self-deporting to Spain, sources tell ABC News.

item.title: New York jury convicts Huawei of stealing trade secrets
item.description: A New York jury has found Chinese telecom giant Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets and other criminal offences, but acquitted it of a racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. The verdict followed a three-month trial in New York in a case that adds to longstanding US efforts to curb Huawei's operations over alleged threats to national security.

item.title: Potential health effects of Army's detonation of nearly 5 tons of lead azide
item.description: The U.S. Army is planning a controlled detonation of explosive material at an ammunition plant in rural Iowa on Wednesday. There could be potential health effects.

item.title: Champions League: Real Madrid thrash PSV 5-1 in comeback win as Manchester City held by Napoli
item.description: Real Madrid extended their winning run to 10 games in all competitions on Tuesday, overturning an early deficit to rout PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League, with Jude Bellingham scoring a spectacular goal and Kylian Mbappé netting twice. Manchester City, meanwhile, twice came from behind to draw 2-2 with Napoli, while Arsenal were held to a 1-1 draw by Borussia Dortmund.

item.title: WATCH: President Trump holds Thanksgiving turkey pardoning ceremony
item.description: President Donald Trump held the annual Thanksgiving turkey pardon ceremony at the White House on Tuesday.

item.title: Tech executives' investment in Trump 'clearly paying off' as Huang reinstated at Nvidia
item.description: Nvidia shares fell on Tuesday as the historic rally sparked by Jensen Huang's return as CEO quickly lost steam, with investors refocusing ​on the political ‌and governance risks surrounding his reinstatement. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, The Hill Senior Technology Reporter Miranda Nazzaro says that the reinstatement of Jensen Huang at Nvidia represents "the culmination of a two-year push of tech executives to get closer to President Trump and their investment in the President is clearly paying off".

item.title: WATCH: Viral 'DWTS' fans talk season 35 finale
item.description: Superfans Giorgina Martino and Alex Foley and their baby London join ABC News Live to discuss the finale and what they think are some of the most shocking moments from the season.

item.title: 'Quid pro quo’: Nvidia too big to fail or ‘too close to personal interest of people around Trump’?
item.description: Angela Diffley is pleased to welcome Bernard Benhamou, Secretary General of the Institute of Digital Sovereignty and Senior Lecturer in Internet Governance at Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne University. What does Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia mean for Trump, Lutnick, the US, the AI industry and China? Describing Huang as “the global banker of the AI industry”, Benhamou explains: “He is the visionary, he is the banker. He's not only the chip maker.” He also warns of the repercussions of Donald Trump's decision to reinstate the Nvidia CEO, with congressional and judicial scrutiny looming. “It's far from over. It's just the beginning.”

item.title: Trump awards Medal of Freedom to former NYC Mayor Rudy Giuliani
item.description: Trump pardoned Giuliani last year.

item.title: Armed men take hostages in Colombia tourist hotspot
item.description: A group of armed men are holding at least 25 people hostage in a supermarket in Colombia, according to officials.

item.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia comeback sends AI videos into overdrive
item.description: Just 11 days after resigning as Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang’s return has unleashed a fresh wave of AI-generated videos. But the internet has changed its tune: while last week’s memes mocked Huang, many now celebrate his comeback. One viral video purportedly showing him dancing is actually AI-manipulated footage of a basketball coach from 2016. From humiliation to hero worship, the technology Nvidia helped popularise is rewriting the narrative surrounding its own CEO, as Vedika Bahl explains.

item.title: Attorney General Blanche sidesteps questions about DOJ probe into Nvidia's Huang
item.description: Blanche described Nvidia as "a good corporate citizen."

item.title: Did Nvidia knowingly send chips to China 'cutout'? Was there ‘pay-to-play’ involving Trump, Lutnick?
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Andrew Weissmann, Professor of Practice at NYU School of Law and a former federal prosecutor known for leading major Department of Justice (DOJ) and FBI investigations. “Why were they treating Nvidia so favorably? Professor Weissmann joins us to discuss the legal and ethical questions surrounding the Trump administration's dealings with the chipmaker. He examines allegations of personal financial gain, the implications for US national security, the limits of presidential immunity and what he describes as an “unholy alliance of tech bros, of Wall Street, and of politicians."

item.title: Senegal reinstated as AFCON 2025 winners
item.description: In tonight's edition, Senegal were reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners after the sport's highest court upheld their appeal against being stripped of the title.

item.title: Huawei guilty of plotting to steal trade secrets and bank fraud
item.description: Chinese tech giant Huawei, has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud after a landmark trial in the US.

item.title: UN slams Iran after it flogs singer for performing without veil
item.description: The United Nations condemned as "abhorrent" the flogging of Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her production team, urging Tehran to abolish the practice. The five received 74 lashes each on Monday following a performance viewed millions of times on YouTube, local media reported, citing Ahmadi's lawyer.

item.title: They want to watch Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan die but the Army won’t let them
item.description: Julia Wilson was nine months pregnant when she found herself caught in gunfire at Fort Hood in 2009. 'It's crazy how quickly things run through your brain," she said.

item.title: Groups push back on Trump administration changes to historical monument
item.description: Two Philadelphia groups filed a federal lawsuit against the Trump administration over the removal of panels at the slavery memorial at the President’s House site.

item.title: Russian nuclear satellites plan 'foolhardy', expert says
item.description: NATO chief Mark Rutte said Monday the alliance would defend against threats in space when asked about German media reports that Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Jennie Shin, Dafydd Townley, Senior Teaching Fellow in International Security at the University of Portsmouth, says that the alleged plan would be "foolhardy because the impact would be indiscriminate, they wouldn't be able to choose only Western or non-Russian satellites".

item.title: The Bukele method: will Salvadoran leader's strong-arm tactics work for Haiti?
item.description: Haitians are hailing the Bukele method. Citizens of the Americas’ poorest nation cheering the Salvadoran president’s ’shoot first, ask questions later’ method of dealing with the gangs that have overrun their country the past six years. Can the police force deployed actually restore law and order? We’ll ask about the latest in a decades-long list of efforts by the international community to support Haiti.

item.title: Senegal AFCON ruling 'good in the books of sports law', expert says
item.description: Speaking with FRANCE 24's Jennie Shin, sports presenter and journalist Thando Sibiya explains that the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport to reinstate Senegal as ⁠winner of ​the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations "from a jurisprudence perspective or creating precedent, it is going to be good in the books of sports law, because if every single decision of a referee is taken to a court of law all the time, it really tampers with the quality, governance and legitimacy of the game".

item.title: Senegal regain AFCON title on appeal at Morocco's expense
item.description: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. CAS said in a statement it had "upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF)" by a "unanimous decision". FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

item.title: Car bomb destroys buildings in central Colombian city
item.description: A car bomb detonated in the central Colombian city of Villavicencio on Monday, destroying a local governor's office and surrounding buildings, President Abelardo de la Espriella said. The right-wing leader has conducted a major crackdown on the country's drug trade, in response to left-wing FARC rebels who have stepped up attacks over the past two years. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Russian losses on Ukrainian front top 700,000 including missing
item.description: New analysis of leaked Russian government data suggests more than 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in the war against Ukraine. Independent Russian media outlets have updated their estimates of Moscow's military casualties, including soldiers missing on the frontline, after Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers obtained figures from the Russian statistics agency. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland explains.

item.title: 'Unknown substance' released at rap concert could be linked to 'robberies', police say
item.description: The "unknown substance" that sparked a mass evacuation at a rap concert could be linked to robberies and reports of jewellery being stolen, police say.

item.title: Canada's defense minister says his country answers to no one in Washington
item.description: Canada’s defense minister says that his country answers to no one in Washington, asserting Canadian sovereignty after the Pentagon accused Ottawa of failing to meet its military commitments

item.title: Thomas Markle formally charged in US over possessing child sexual abuse material
item.description: Thomas Markle has been indicted on two counts of possessing child sexual abuse material in Los Angeles.

item.title: Gunmen hold 25 people hostage at supermarket in Colombia's Cartagena
item.description: Armed robbers took 25 people hostage at a supermarket in Colombia’s tourist city of Cartagena on Tuesday, prompting a major police operation and a temporary suspension of incoming flights, authorities said. Landings at Rafael Nunez International Airport resumed after the military used a runway during the operation.

item.title: Russia's war on Ukraine: 'Both sides are prepared to operate outside of the conflict zone'
item.description: Charli James is pleased to welcome Gavin Hall, Teaching Fellow in Political Science, and International Security at the University of Strathclyde. Hall examines recent Russian and Ukrainian operations beyond the main conflict zone, the conditions necessary for a negotiated settlement and the implications of diminishing direct US military support for Ukraine. “Both sides are prepared to operate beyond the main battleground and outside of the conflict zone,” he explains. Hall discusses why both sides want to negotiate from a position of strength and the conditions under which a “mutually hurting stalemate” could lead to a negotiated settlement.

item.title: Anthropic plunges below IPO price in renewed tech sell-off
item.description: Anthropic shares have fallen sharply in a renewed tech-led sell-off, taking the stock well below its initial public offering (IPO) level of just last week.

item.title: Yemen’s army says Houthi fighters closing in on government stronghold of Aden
item.description: Yemen's military on Tuesday said that Houthi fighters were closing in on the internationally recognised government's stronghold of Aden from about 60km (40 miles) away and vowed to repel any assault. A military spokesman said defences were prepared following Houthi advances and government pullbacks near the Red Sea.

item.title: WATCH: Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys celebrate 30 years of giving back
item.description: ABC News' Rhiannon Ally highlights how the Dallas Cowboys are celebrating three decades of giving back to their community during Thanksgiving.

item.title: France's ex-president Nicolas Sarkozy, wife Carla Bruni to stand trial for alleged witness tampering
item.description: France's former president Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, singer Carla Bruni-Sarkozy, are set to be tried in 2027 on charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as benefitting from witness tampering. The new charges are related to the Sarkozy couple's actions during the case examining illegal campaign funding from Libyan strongman Muammar Gaddafi over which Sarkozy was imprisoned last year.

item.title: 'We are ready to facilitate removal of Netanyahu': Head of Israel's Arab-majority Joint List
item.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, the head of the Arab-majority Joint List said his political alliance is prepared to play a decisive role in bringing down Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government following the recent election. "We are ready to facilitate the removal of Netanyahu" from power, Yousef Jabareen said, signalling a willingness to explore political alliances beyond traditional divisions in Israeli politics.

item.title: Senegal reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners
item.description: Senegal ​were reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners ​on Tuesday after the Court of Arbitration for Sport upheld their appeal against being stripped of the title. Senegal contested the ​Confederation ‌of African Football's decision to declare ⁠Morocco champions, despite Senegal beating the hosts 1-0 after extra time in ‌January's final in Rabat. Morocco announced that it would “pursue all necessary legal procedures” in response to the decision.

item.title: Police fear missing woman 'may have come to harm' as man in court charged with murder
item.description: A man has appeared in court charged with murder after detectives investigating the disappearance of a young woman said they have to "consider the possibility that she may have come to harm".

item.title: London Underground strike to go ahead after talks break down
item.description: A 24-hour strike by London Tube drivers is set to go ahead this week after talks failed to resolve the dispute.

item.title: 'Tis the season to be green: Can the Christmas holidays be a present for the planet?
item.description: With the holiday season just around the corner, we take a look at its environmental impact. We discuss how to make Christmas a little greener as consumers, whether plastic trees or natural ones are better for the planet, and what small steps we can all take to reduce our carbon footprint during the festivities.

item.title: WATCH: Detroit Lions help feed their community this Thanksgiving
item.description: ABC News' Will Reeve shares how the Detroit Lions are carrying on a Thanksgiving tradition of giving back to those in need.

item.title: French police officer who shot teenager to face murder trial
item.description: A French police officer will stand trial for murder in the killing of a teenager in 2023 that sparked violent protests across the country, the Versailles appeals court said on Tuesday. Nahel Merzouk, 17, was shot in the Paris suburb of Nanterre after he failed to comply with an order to stop his car.

item.title: Leaked data suggests 500,000 Russian soldiers killed since start of Ukraine invasion
item.description: More than 500,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war with Ukraine, according to an estimate by a number of media organisations. The figures are based on a huge dataset that was hacked from Russia’s state statistics agency Rosstat by Belarusian activist group Cyber Partisans and a Ukrainian hacker group, Silent Crow. Two independent Russian news outlets Meduza and Mediazona say the death toll may rise to more than 700,000 once missing soldiers are included.

item.title: Army says lead explosives detonation will proceed after court denies bid to stop it
item.description: Trump said he wants the OK from the federal appeals court and incoming Iowa governor to proceed.

item.title: Who really owns the Albanian land Jared Kushner wants to turn into a 5-star resort?
item.description: Albania's Prime Minister Edi Rama has vowed that Kushner's resort project will go ahead as planned. But an ongoing investigation by Albania's state prosecutor into forged land titles could halt the project.

item.title: Trump granted new chance to potentially erase his hush money case
item.description: An appeals court is giving President Trump a new chance to move his criminal hush money case into federal court, where he could then attempt to overturn his conviction.

item.title: Trump owned at least $12 million in Nvidia stock at the end of last year
item.description: President Donald Trump owned at least $12 million in Nvidia stock at the end of 2025, according to his annual financial disclosure report reviewed by ABC News.

item.title: WATCH: Amazon drone crash raises safety concerns
item.description: The FAA Is investigating after an Amazon delivery drone crashed onto a garage near Detroit after dropping off a package.

item.title: WATCH: 'Dancing with the Stars' watch parties on tap for live season finale
item.description: Millions of "Dancing with the Stars" fans are already warming up their popcorn poppers and fondue pots -- with others turning the show's finale into an epic night out.

item.description: China has sentenced to death an official who was said to have leaked state secrets to a foreign country.

item.title: FA chair had to sign NDA to view FIFA documents on World Cup sell-off
item.description: Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt has now viewed some FIFA documents on the World Cup sell-off but had to sign a nondisclosure agreement, Sky News has learned.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir shares how NFL teams are giving back this Thanksgiving
item.description: As millions prepare for a day of thanks this holiday season, NFL teams across America are serving meals to their communities this Thanksgiving.

item.title: What should it cost to insure a home in wildfire country?
item.description: Some California homeowners have spent thousands making their homes safer from wildfires. Yet all that work has barely made a dent in their insurance bills. Should they be getting a bigger break?

item.title: Two men arrested over suspected burglary at William and Kate's home
item.description: Two men have been arrested over a suspected burglary at William and Kate's Norfolk home.

item.description: Two turkeys named Freedom and Feather are set to get Thanksgiving pardons from President Donald Trump Tuesday.

item.title: Rep. Jimmy Gomez to resign after House Ethics report he engaged in sexual misconduct
item.description: Gomez lost his reelection bid in November.

item.title: Doctors struggle to save babies after parents refuse vitamin K
item.description: Doctors are fighting an uphill battle against disinformation about routine vitamin K shots given to newborns in the hospital. It helps prevent a rare but devastating bleeding disorder.

item.title: They attended Trump's meme coin dinner. It didn't go well
item.description: Trump's meme coin dinners have sparked intense controversy. These two guests attended his latest on Sunday — and agreed to provide NPR inside access.

item.title: Black travelers on Route 66 weren't welcome at most gas stations — except this one
item.description: Threatt Filling Station in Luther, Okla., was the first Black-owned gas station on Route 66. At a time when Black families needed the Green Book to find places to stay, eat, use the bathroom, it provided fuel and respite.

item.title: For workplace culture champions, Jensen Huang's return is 'unfathomable'
item.description: Some who have worked to promote diversity and inclusion in Silicon Valley say Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO sends a message that all that matters is money.

item.title: The human cost of the electric vehicle boom is at the center of a lawsuit in Congo
item.description: A landmark lawsuit in Congo sees 27 residents accuse a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine of poisoning their community and the government of failing to protect them.

item.title: WATCH: As the holiday season nears, experts warn against so-called porch pirates
item.description: Millions of packages are stolen each year, but AI tools and porch cameras can help prevent theft.

item.title: Morocco 'astonished' at decision to restore Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations champions
item.description: Senegal have been awarded the Africa Cup of Nations title after successfully appealing against the decision to strip them of it.

item.description: The storm set to slam New York City could ground Macy's parade balloons for the first time in 55 years.

item.description: Gisele Pelicot has said she is "deeply shocked" and "humiliated" after nude images of her were sent to the media without her consent to promote a new book about coercive control.

item.description: Navy officials had weighed renaming the vessel for Trump, sources said.

item.description: The ESPN legend and former All-Pro linebacker died at 75.

item.title: WATCH: How AI tools can help lock in the lowest prices for holiday shopping
item.description: More than 40% of consumers have used AI assistants for online shopping, according to Adobe, and ABC News’ Becky Worley tried them to see how they can help with your shopping.

item.title: Deadly fire at confectionery factory kills 24 as rescuers search for dozens still missing
item.description: A deadly fire that tore through a confectionery factory in Indonesia has claimed the lives of 24 people, with 34 others still missing.

item.title: Man who was lured to remote villa and held for 15 hours rescued after being tied up and beaten
item.description: A man has been rescued after he was lured to an isolated villa, held for 15 hours, tied to a chair, beaten, and threatened with death, police in Spain say.
